name: Old Serra'kis
summary: Beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum, Old Serra'kis lurks in the flooded depths of Blackfathom Deeps. The enormous threshadon is hidden in a submerged cave, and deadly to anyone who seeks him there.

sections.title: Unconquered in the Depths
sections.body: The Twilight's Hammer has made its home in the sunken Moonshrine Ruins. Beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum, dark waters conceal older, wilder things. Old Serra'kis, the largest threshadon in the sunken temple, lurks in the Forgotten Pool, a flooded cave beneath the ruins where few would think to look.

sections.title: A Hidden Threat
sections.body: To reach Old Serra'kis, you must dive deep beneath the temple floor into a flooded cavern. No air pockets break the water, making the cave as deadly as the beast within. Cornered in the murk, Serra'kis shows an unnatural resilience. He drains life from his attackers with shadow energy, sustaining his own vitality in the darkness.

faq.q: What kind of creature is Old Serra'kis?
faq.answer: Old Serra'kis is a massive, ancient threshadon, a long-necked aquatic reptile native to Azeroth's lakes and coastal waters.

faq.q: Why didn't the Twilight's Hammer kill him?
faq.answer: Nothing records the cult hunting him. Old Serra'kis hides in the Forgotten Pool, a flooded, airless cave beneath the ruins, and is deadly to anyone who dives in after him.
Old Serra'kis lurks in a submerged cavern beneath the water around the Moonshrine Sanctum in Blackfathom Deeps. You must dive under the ruins into an airless pool to encounter him.
The fight takes place underwater, with no natural air pockets. Old Serra'kis leeches shadow energy from nearby foes to heal his wounds throughout the battle.

faq.q: Does Serra'kis serve the Twilight's Hammer?
faq.answer: No. Unlike other beasts corrupted or trained by the cult, Old Serra'kis remains an untamed wild predator defending his subterranean lair.

faq.q: Can you breathe during the battle with Serra'kis?
faq.answer: The enclosed cave has no air pockets near the ceiling. Underwater fighters must manage their breath, use magical water-breathing aid, or draw the beast toward open water.

angles.text: As a druid of the wild, Aquatic Form helps you dive into the lightless pool to confront this prehistoric predator.
As a warlock, you can bestow Unending Breath, making an airless subterranean ambush manageable.
As a shaman, you can use Water Breathing spells granted through communion with the elements to help your companions avoid drowning as they grapple with the ancient threshadon.
